title: An independent set of size 1129 in the sixth strong power of C7
description:
A machine-checkable certificate for α(C7⊠6) ≥ 1129, improving the previously best known value 1120 (Itty, Rosin, Carstensen, Reichman, arXiv:2607.21517, Table 5, Appendix B), which itself improved the elementary product 1101 = 367 · 3.

The archive contains the certificate (1129 vertices of C7⊠6, one per line as six digits), a second certificate of size 1128, and two dependency-free verifiers sharing no code (Node.js and Python 3), each performing the naive all-pairs test so that it can be audited by reading it.

This improves a table entry, not the Shannon capacity bound: matching the current record Θ(C7) ≥ 3.25883262 with a single sixth-power set would require 1198, and 1129^(1/6) = 3.22687635. The note also records that the set is invariant under the single-layer and adjacent-pair large-neighbourhood moves in all six coordinate directions, evidence that it is a ceiling for this method rather than an artefact of a truncated search.

The local search, the note and both verifiers were carried out with the assistance of a large language model. The result does not rest on that: what is claimed is a single list of 1129 vertices, and either verifier settles it outright by the naive all-pairs test, which is slow but short enough to audit by reading. A certificate is true or false on its own terms, whatever produced it.
